info.bio:
Penguins is the project of Melbourne based artist and Vacant Valley owner Peter Bramley. 

Since 2007, Penguins has ranged from pop/electronic to intense/odd solo work to heavy noise rock band mode.

Other members: 
Damian Clarkson (ex St Helens), Tam Matlakowski (Pop Singles), Michael O'Dwyer (War Pigs) and David Freudenstein (Grand Prismatic).

scenes.name: Rock'n'roll
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Fusión de rhythm'n'blues y country, con mucho más peso del primero. Chuck Berry inventa en 1955 el rock'n'roll tal como se conocerá durante cincuenta años (la guitarra como instrumento protagonista, canciones propias que hablan a los adolescentes); Bo Diddley aporta el ritmo «hambone», Little Richard y Esquerita el histerismo y el maquillaje (el primer «decadence-rock»), Jerry Lee Lewis el piano feroz y Sun Records el rockabilly. Elvis Presley es, para Scaruffi, «la primera gran estafa del rock'n'roll». Buddy Holly y Eddie Cochran abren otra vía; en paralelo nacen el soul (Ray Charles), la exótica (Martin Denny, Esquivel), la música electrónica de cinta y, en Gran Bretaña, el skiffle.

podcast.title: Connection to John Dolphin
podcast.body: John Dolphin, owner of Dolphins of Hollywood, was discussed in previous podcast episodes concerning Jean and Eunice and The Penguins, indicating his significant role in their success. "We've talked about Dolphin before, in the episodes on Jean and Eunice and the Penguins."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Contrast to The Famous Flames' Style
podcast.body: The Penguins embodied a "smooth, sophisticated sound" in R&B, which stood in contrast to the energetic and viscerally emotional approach that The Famous Flames were cultivating. "They were going for energy and for pure expression of visceral emotion, rather than the smooth, sophisticated sounds of the Platters or Penguins."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Impact of Gaynell Hodge
podcast.body: Gaynell Hodge was a crucial figure in the 1950s LA vocal group scene, and his contributions were so fundamental that without him, groups like The Penguins would not have existed. "without him there would have been no platters, penguins, or Jesse Bellvin."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Leverage for The Platters' Signing
podcast.body: The Penguins, having just scored their only big hit with "Earth Angel," were managed by Book Ram. Mercury Records was keen to sign them, but Ram agreed only on the condition that Mercury also signed The Platters, effectively using The Penguins' success as leverage for his preferred group. "Ram agreed to the deal, but only on the condition that Mercury signed the platters as well."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Members Joined Cornel Gunter's Coasters
podcast.body: Three members of Cornel Gunter's newly formed "The Coasters" group had previously been members of The Penguins. Gunter himself had emerged from the same musical "stew" of vocal groups as The Penguins and had known them for years. "A more accurate name might have been The Penguins since the other three members of his new group had been members of The Penguins previously."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Ram's Disinterest After Signing
podcast.body: After successfully using The Penguins to secure a deal for The Platters with Mercury Records, Book Ram largely abandoned The Penguins, who subsequently never achieved any further success. "Once they were signed, Ram largely gave up on the penguins, who never had any further success."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
